fact: Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021, enacted 24 March 2021, sets conditions in Part X (sections 70-71) for sending personal data outside the Republic: data subject consent plus Commissioner-approved standard contracts or intragroup schemes, or a Ministerial prescription of permissible transfers on an adequate-level-of-protection test, or Commissioner approval of a transfer in necessity; sensitive personal data must stay in the Republic; the Act itself says it commences on a date the Minister appoints by statutory instrument, and the document gives no commencement date.

The D4D Hub research paper states that Zambia's Data Protection Act No. 3 of 2021 requires sensitive personal data (health records, biometrics, religious beliefs, political opinions) to be stored within the country, quoting Section 70 that sensitive personal data can only be stored in Zambia and other personal data goes on servers in the Republic unless transfer is approved.

The African Union's treaty status list of 8 July 2024 records Zambia as having ratified the Convention on Cyber Security and Personal Data Protection on 15 December 2020 and deposited its instrument on 24 March 2021.
